introduction: The `gitcmd` package (`internal/gitcmd/`) is a foundational Go library that wraps `exec.Command` with hardened security defaults and structured error handling for executing git subprocesses within the af-hub platform. It provides the `GitRunner` struct, `BranchExists` method, `CheckGitVersion` function, and `GitError` type used by the merge queue, continuous rebase, and campaign operations.

glossary.BranchExists: A method on *GitRunner that uses git ls-remote --exit-code to determine whether a branch exists on a remote, with three-way exit code discrimination.
glossary.CheckGitVersion: A package-level function that validates the host git binary meets the minimum version requirement (2.38) at startup.
glossary.GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL: An environment variable that restricts which git transport protocols are permitted; set to 'file:https:ssh' as a security invariant.
glossary.GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM: An environment variable that causes git to ignore system-level git configuration when set to '1'.
glossary.GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT: An environment variable that disables interactive credential prompts when set to '0', preventing the hub process from hanging.
glossary.GitError: A structured error type returned by Run on non-zero git exit codes, containing the Command (args without binary prefix), ExitCode, and Stderr fields.
glossary.GitRunner: A struct in internal/gitcmd/ that wraps exec.Command with safety environment defaults and a fixed working directory, used to execute git subprocesses.
glossary.NewRunner: The constructor function for GitRunner, accepting a working directory and optional additional environment variable key=value strings.
glossary.RunExitCode: A method on *GitRunner that executes a git command and returns the raw exit code separately, used for commands where non-zero exit codes carry specific semantics.
glossary.SIGKILL: The signal sent by exec.CommandContext to a subprocess when the context is cancelled or times out, terminating it immediately without a graceful shutdown window.
glossary.deduplication step: The process by which GitRunner removes earlier occurrences of safety-default keys from the inherited and caller-supplied environment before appending the safety defaults, ensuring the safety values always win.
glossary.internal/gitcmd/: The Go package path for the gitcmd package within the af-hub module.
glossary.ls-remote: A git subcommand that queries a remote repository for its refs without cloning; used by BranchExists with --exit-code for three-way discrimination.
glossary.merge-tree: A git subcommand (git merge-tree --write-tree) used by the merge queue to perform in-index merges; requires git >= 2.38.
glossary.refs/heads/: The git ref namespace prefix for branch references; BranchExists always prepends this to the bare branch name before passing to git ls-remote.
glossary.safety defaults: The three hardcoded environment variables (GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM) always appended last to every exec.Cmd environment, overriding any inherited or caller-supplied values.
glossary.workDir: The working directory field of GitRunner, set at construction time and used as the working directory for all subprocess invocations.

user_story.goal: construct a GitRunner with a working directory and optional extra environment variables
user_story.benefit: so that all subsequent git subprocess calls inherit safety defaults without per-call configuration

acceptance_criteria.action: construct and return an immutable *GitRunner with workDir set, the caller-supplied env strings stored, and safety defaults configured for appending on every invocation
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns *GitRunner; no error is returned; no validation of workDir existence is performed at construction time
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes NewRunner with a workDir string and zero or more key=value env strings

acceptance_criteria.action: build every exec.Cmd environment by concatenating os.Environ(), then caller-supplied env strings, then safety defaults, after removing any earlier occurrences of GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT, and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM keys via the deduplication step
set GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL to 'file:https:ssh', GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT to '0', and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM to '1' as the final entries in every exec.Cmd environment, hardcoded and not overridable by any caller
be safe for concurrent use by multiple goroutines calling Run or RunExitCode simultaneously, with no mutable shared state after construction

edge_cases.action: strip the caller-supplied value during the deduplication step and replace it with the hardcoded safety default value
edge_cases.return_contract: returns *GitRunner; the safety default value wins; the caller-supplied value is silently discarded
edge_cases.error_condition: a caller passes a key=value string for a safety-default key (e.g. GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=1) in the env parameter

edge_cases.action: construct the GitRunner with an empty workDir; no error is returned at construction time; the raw os/exec error is returned if Run or RunExitCode is later called and the working directory is invalid
edge_cases.return_contract: returns *GitRunner with empty workDir; construction succeeds
edge_cases.trigger: a caller invokes NewRunner with an empty string for workDir

edge_cases.action: construct the GitRunner with only the inherited os.Environ() and safety defaults in the environment; no caller env entries are added
edge_cases.return_contract: returns *GitRunner; safety defaults are still applied
edge_cases.trigger: a caller invokes NewRunner with no additional env strings

requirements.title: Run method — execute git command with structured error

user_story.goal: execute a git subcommand and receive stdout, stderr, and a structured error on failure
user_story.benefit: so that git failures are uniformly formatted and diagnosable from logs

acceptance_criteria.action: execute 'git <args>' in workDir with the constructed environment, capture stdout and stderr, and return them along with nil error on exit code 0
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes Run with a context and one or more args

acceptance_criteria.action: return a *GitError with Command set to the joined args string (without the 'git' binary prefix), ExitCode set to the exit code, and Stderr set to the captured stderr string
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns (stdout []byte, stderr []byte, *GitError) where GitError.Error() produces 'git <args> exited with code <N>: <stderr>'
acceptance_criteria.error_condition: git exits with a non-zero exit code

acceptance_criteria.action: return the raw *exec.Error from os/exec directly without wrapping it in a GitError
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns (nil, nil, *exec.Error) — no GitError is produced for host misconfiguration
acceptance_criteria.error_condition: the git binary is not found on PATH

acceptance_criteria.action: send SIGKILL to the subprocess immediately (Go exec.CommandContext default), return whatever partial stdout and stderr bytes were buffered before cancellation, and return the context error
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns (partialStdout []byte, partialStderr []byte, error) where err wraps the context cancellation or deadline exceeded error; both err != nil and len(stdout) > 0 may be true simultaneously
acceptance_criteria.error_condition: the context is cancelled or times out before the subprocess completes

edge_cases.action: invoke 'git' with no subcommand; git prints a usage message to stderr and exits non-zero; return the resulting GitError without any additional programmer-mistake guard
edge_cases.return_contract: returns (nil or empty stdout, stderr bytes, *GitError) with git's usage message in Stderr
edge_cases.trigger: a caller invokes Run with no args

edge_cases.action: return the raw os/exec error from exec.Cmd.Run without wrapping it in a GitError
edge_cases.return_contract: returns (nil, nil, error) where error is the raw os/exec working-directory error
edge_cases.error_condition: workDir does not exist when Run is called

edge_cases.action: return partial stdout and stderr alongside the context error; the caller is responsible for handling the case where both err != nil and len(stdout) > 0
edge_cases.return_contract: returns (partialStdout []byte, partialStderr []byte, error) — partial output is not discarded
edge_cases.error_condition: the subprocess is killed by SIGKILL due to context cancellation and has produced partial output

requirements.title: RunExitCode method — raw exit code with system-error discrimination

user_story.goal: execute a git command and receive the raw exit code separately from system-level errors
user_story.benefit: so that non-zero exit codes with specific semantics (e.g. ls-remote exit 2) can be interpreted correctly without being conflated with system failures

acceptance_criteria.action: return stdout, stderr, the raw exit code, and nil error; the exit code is meaningful regardless of whether it is zero or non-zero
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns (stdout []byte, stderr []byte, exitCode int, nil) where exitCode reflects the subprocess exit status
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes RunExitCode with a context and args, and the subprocess completes (including non-zero exit)

acceptance_criteria.action: return err != nil wrapped via fmt.Errorf("%w", ...) preserving the underlying os/exec error; return the raw exitCode from exec.ExitError.ExitCode() as secondary diagnostic context only
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns (partialStdout []byte, partialStderr []byte, exitCode int, error) where error wraps the underlying os/exec error and is unwrappable via errors.Is/errors.As; no GitError is produced
acceptance_criteria.error_condition: a system-level failure occurs (binary not found, context cancelled, permission denied)

acceptance_criteria.action: return err != nil and exitCode == -1 (Go's exec.ExitError.ExitCode() value for signal termination); return any partial stdout/stderr bytes accumulated before cancellation
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns (partialStdout []byte, partialStderr []byte, -1, error) where error wraps the context cancellation error
acceptance_criteria.error_condition: context cancellation causes SIGKILL and the subprocess is signal-terminated

acceptance_criteria.action: never produce a GitError; system-level failures are wrapped via fmt.Errorf("%w", ...) so callers can use errors.As(err, &GitError{}) to unambiguously distinguish git-level failures (from Run) from system-level failures (from RunExitCode)

edge_cases.action: return err != nil wrapping the *exec.Error; exitCode is the raw value from exec.ExitError.ExitCode() or 0 if no ExitError is available
edge_cases.return_contract: returns (nil, nil, exitCode, error) where errors.As(err, &*exec.Error{}) succeeds
edge_cases.error_condition: the git binary is not found on PATH

edge_cases.action: return err != nil and exitCode == 0 (process never started, no exit code available), consistent with exec.CommandContext behavior
edge_cases.return_contract: returns (nil, nil, 0, error) where error wraps the context cancellation
edge_cases.error_condition: the subprocess has not yet started when the context is cancelled

edge_cases.action: invoke 'git' with no subcommand; git exits non-zero; return the exit code and nil error without a GitError
edge_cases.return_contract: returns (nil or empty stdout, stderr bytes, nonZeroExitCode, nil)
edge_cases.trigger: a caller invokes RunExitCode with no args

requirements.title: BranchExists — three-way exit code discrimination for ls-remote

user_story.goal: determine whether a branch exists on a remote without misinterpreting network or auth failures as branch-missing
user_story.benefit: so that the merge queue does not silently treat a network timeout or auth failure as a missing branch

acceptance_criteria.action: run 'git ls-remote --exit-code <remote> refs/heads/<branch>' and return true, nil indicating the branch exists on the remote
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes BranchExists with a context, remote URL, and bare branch name, and git ls-remote exits with code 0

acceptance_criteria.action: return false, nil indicating the branch is genuinely absent from the remote
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes BranchExists and git ls-remote exits with code 2

acceptance_criteria.action: return false and a non-nil error describing the failure; do not treat this as branch-missing
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns (false, error) where error describes the git failure
acceptance_criteria.error_condition: git ls-remote exits with any non-zero, non-2 exit code (e.g. 1, 128) indicating a network, auth, or system failure

acceptance_criteria.action: always prepend refs/heads/ to the bare branch name before passing to git ls-remote --exit-code; callers must not pass a full ref path

edge_cases.action: return false and a non-nil error; do not return false, nil
edge_cases.return_contract: returns (false, error)
edge_cases.error_condition: the remote URL is invalid or the remote host is unreachable, causing git ls-remote to exit with code 128

edge_cases.action: send SIGKILL to the subprocess and return false and a non-nil error wrapping the context error
edge_cases.return_contract: returns (false, error) where error wraps the context cancellation or deadline exceeded error
edge_cases.error_condition: the context deadline expires or is cancelled while git ls-remote is running against a slow or unreachable remote

edge_cases.action: prepend refs/heads/ regardless, producing 'refs/heads/refs/heads/main', which will not match any real branch and will return false, nil (exit code 2); this is a caller contract violation and the package does not guard against it
edge_cases.return_contract: returns (false, nil) — silently incorrect; callers must pass bare branch names only
edge_cases.error_condition: a caller passes a full ref path (e.g. 'refs/heads/main') as the branch parameter instead of a bare branch name

edge_cases.action: run 'git ls-remote --exit-code <remote> refs/heads/' which will query all branches; the result depends on git's behavior and is not guarded by the package
edge_cases.return_contract: returns (bool, error) based on git ls-remote exit code; behavior is caller-contract violation territory
edge_cases.error_condition: the branch parameter is an empty string

user_story.goal: receive a structured, consistently formatted error from git subprocess failures
user_story.benefit: so that log entries are uniform and callers can programmatically inspect the subcommand, exit code, and stderr

acceptance_criteria.action: implement the error interface with an Error() method that returns a string in the exact format: 'git <Command> exited with code <ExitCode>: <Stderr>'
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: Error() returns a string matching 'git <args> exited with code <N>: <stderr>'

acceptance_criteria.action: store the Command field as the joined args string without the 'git' binary prefix (e.g. 'rebase origin/main'), the ExitCode field as the integer exit code, and the Stderr field as the captured stderr string
be produced exclusively by Run on non-zero exit; RunExitCode must never produce a GitError

edge_cases.action: allow the caller to extract the *GitError and access Command, ExitCode, and Stderr fields programmatically
edge_cases.return_contract: errors.As(err, &gitErr) returns true and populates gitErr with the structured fields
edge_cases.trigger: a caller uses errors.As to inspect an error returned by Run

edge_cases.action: produce the format string 'git <Command> exited with code <ExitCode>: ' with an empty suffix after the colon
edge_cases.return_contract: returns 'git <args> exited with code <N>: '
edge_cases.trigger: the Stderr field is an empty string

requirements.title: CheckGitVersion — minimum version validation at startup

user_story.goal: validate that the host git binary meets the minimum version requirement before starting the merge queue
user_story.benefit: so that misconfigured host environments are detected early with a clear error message rather than producing confusing failures during git operations

acceptance_criteria.action: run 'git --version', parse the version string by extracting the first three dot-separated numeric components, and return nil
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes CheckGitVersion with a context and the installed git version is >= 2.38

acceptance_criteria.action: return an error with the exact format: 'requires git >= 2.38, found <installed>' where <installed> is the parsed version string (e.g. '2.35.1')
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns error with message matching 'requires git >= 2.38, found <version>'
acceptance_criteria.error_condition: the installed git version is below 2.38

acceptance_criteria.action: return a parse error describing the unparseable version string
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns non-nil error describing the parse failure
acceptance_criteria.error_condition: the git --version output cannot be parsed into three numeric components

acceptance_criteria.action: parse the version string by extracting the first three dot-separated numeric components and ignoring trailing tokens, supporting standard ('git version 2.39.1'), Apple Git ('git version 2.39.3 (Apple Git-145)'), and release candidate ('git version 2.38.0.rc1') formats

edge_cases.action: return the raw os/exec error without wrapping it in a GitError
edge_cases.return_contract: returns non-nil error (raw os/exec error)
edge_cases.error_condition: the git binary is not found on PATH

edge_cases.action: return the context error; callers should set a 5-second deadline as recommended
edge_cases.return_contract: returns non-nil error wrapping the context cancellation or deadline exceeded error
edge_cases.error_condition: the context deadline expires or is cancelled while 'git --version' is running

edge_cases.action: extract '2.39.3' as the version by taking only the first three dot-separated numeric components and ignoring the parenthetical suffix
edge_cases.return_contract: returns nil (version meets minimum)
edge_cases.trigger: the version string contains an Apple Git vendor suffix (e.g. 'git version 2.39.3 (Apple Git-145)')

edge_cases.action: extract '2.38.0' as the version by taking only the first three dot-separated numeric components and ignoring the '.rc1' suffix
edge_cases.return_contract: returns nil (version meets minimum)
edge_cases.trigger: the version string contains a release candidate suffix (e.g. 'git version 2.38.0.rc1')

edge_cases.action: return a parse error; do not attempt to compare a partial version
edge_cases.return_contract: returns non-nil error describing the parse failure
edge_cases.error_condition: the version string contains fewer than three dot-separated numeric components

user_story.goal: ensure that safety-default environment variables cannot be overridden by inherited process environment or caller-supplied values
user_story.benefit: so that protocol injection, interactive prompt hangs, and system config interference are prevented regardless of the host environment

acceptance_criteria.action: before passing the environment slice to exec.Cmd.Env, remove all occurrences of GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT, and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM from the inherited os.Environ() and caller-supplied env entries, then append the hardcoded safety defaults as the final entries
set GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL to the hardcoded value 'file:https:ssh' on every invocation; this value is a security invariant and is never configurable at construction time, call time, or any other point

edge_cases.action: strip the inherited value during the deduplication step and replace it with the hardcoded safety default 'file:https:ssh'
edge_cases.return_contract: the subprocess environment contains only GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=file:https:ssh; the inherited value is silently discarded
edge_cases.error_condition: the inherited process environment (os.Environ()) contains GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL set to a different value (e.g. 'ext::')

edge_cases.action: remove all such entries before appending the single hardcoded safety default value
edge_cases.return_contract: the subprocess environment contains exactly one occurrence of each safety-default key with the hardcoded value; all duplicates are stripped
edge_cases.error_condition: the inherited process environment contains multiple entries for the same safety-default key

correctness_properties.title: Safety defaults always win over inherited and caller-supplied env
correctness_properties.for_any: GitRunner constructed with any workDir and any env strings, executing any git command
correctness_properties.invariant: the exec.Cmd.Env slice passed to every subprocess always contains GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL='file:https:ssh', GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT='0', and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM='1' as the final entries, regardless of what os.Environ() or the caller-supplied env strings contain for those keys

correctness_properties.title: GitError is produced by Run if and only if git exits non-zero
correctness_properties.for_any: any call to GitRunner.Run with any args
correctness_properties.invariant: Run returns a non-nil *GitError if and only if the git subprocess exits with a non-zero exit code; it never returns a GitError for system-level failures (binary not found, context cancelled)

correctness_properties.title: RunExitCode never produces a GitError
correctness_properties.for_any: any call to GitRunner.RunExitCode with any args and any context
correctness_properties.invariant: RunExitCode never returns a *GitError; all errors returned by RunExitCode are wrapped via fmt.Errorf("%w", ...) and are unwrappable to the underlying os/exec error

correctness_properties.title: BranchExists exit-2 is the only non-error false return
correctness_properties.for_any: any call to GitRunner.BranchExists with any remote and branch
correctness_properties.invariant: BranchExists returns (false, nil) if and only if git ls-remote exits with code 2; any other non-zero exit code returns (false, non-nil error); exit code 0 returns (true, nil)

correctness_properties.title: GitError.Error() format is always consistent
correctness_properties.for_any: any *GitError with any Command, ExitCode, and Stderr values
correctness_properties.invariant: GitError.Error() always returns a string matching the pattern 'git <Command> exited with code <ExitCode>: <Stderr>' with no deviation in formatting

correctness_properties.title: CheckGitVersion error message format is exact
correctness_properties.invariant: CheckGitVersion returns an error whose message exactly matches 'requires git >= 2.38, found <installed>' where <installed> is the parsed version string

correctness_properties.title: refs/heads/ prefix is always prepended by BranchExists
correctness_properties.for_any: any bare branch name passed to BranchExists
correctness_properties.invariant: the git ls-remote command always receives 'refs/heads/<branch>' as the ref argument, never the bare branch name directly

correctness_properties.title: Concurrent Run and RunExitCode calls are data-race free
correctness_properties.for_any: any number of goroutines calling Run or RunExitCode on the same *GitRunner simultaneously
correctness_properties.invariant: no data races occur; the runner's internal state is immutable after construction and each call creates an independent exec.Cmd

correctness_properties.title: Version parsing extracts exactly three numeric components
correctness_properties.for_any: any git --version output string on supported platforms (standard, Apple Git, release candidate)
correctness_properties.invariant: CheckGitVersion extracts exactly the first three dot-separated numeric components and ignores all trailing tokens; it never uses more or fewer components for the version comparison

execution_paths.title: Happy path: Run executes git rebase and returns output

steps.action: calls GitRunner.Run(ctx, 'rebase', 'origin/main') on a GitRunner constructed with NewRunner(workDir)
builds exec.Cmd environment by concatenating os.Environ(), caller env, then safety defaults after deduplication step
executes 'git rebase origin/main' in workDir with the constructed environment
captures stdout and stderr from the subprocess
returns (stdout []byte, stderr []byte, nil) to the merge queue caller on exit code 0

execution_paths.title: Failure path: Run returns GitError on non-zero exit

steps.action: calls GitRunner.Run(ctx, 'rebase', 'origin/main')
executes 'git rebase origin/main' in workDir
exits with non-zero exit code and writes conflict message to stderr
constructs *GitError with Command='rebase origin/main', ExitCode=1, Stderr=captured stderr
returns (stdout []byte, stderr []byte, *GitError) to the merge queue caller; GitError.Error() produces 'git rebase origin/main exited with code 1: <stderr>'
calls GitRunner.BranchExists(ctx, 'https://github.com/org/repo', 'feature/foo')
prepends refs/heads/ to form 'refs/heads/feature/foo' and calls RunExitCode(ctx, 'ls-remote', '--exit-code', remote, 'refs/heads/feature/foo')
executes 'git ls-remote --exit-code <remote> refs/heads/feature/foo' with safety defaults applied
exits with code 0, writing the ref line to stdout
returns (true, nil) to the merge queue caller
calls GitRunner.BranchExists(ctx, remoteURL, 'nonexistent-branch')
calls RunExitCode(ctx, 'ls-remote', '--exit-code', remoteURL, 'refs/heads/nonexistent-branch')
exits with code 2 (branch not found)
returns (false, nil) to the merge queue caller
calls GitRunner.BranchExists(ctx, 'https://invalid.example.com/repo', 'main')
calls RunExitCode(ctx, 'ls-remote', '--exit-code', remoteURL, 'refs/heads/main')
exits with code 128 (connection failure)
detects exit code is non-zero and non-2, constructs an error describing the failure
returns (false, error) to the merge queue caller; caller does not misinterpret this as branch-missing

execution_paths.title: CheckGitVersion: valid version at hub startup

steps.action: calls CheckGitVersion(ctx) with a 5-second deadline context before starting the merge queue
executes 'git --version' via os/exec
outputs 'git version 2.39.1' and exits with code 0
parses '2.39.1' from the output by extracting the first three dot-separated numeric components
compares 2.39.1 >= 2.38 and returns nil to the hub startup routine
calls CheckGitVersion(ctx) during initialization
executes 'git --version' and receives 'git version 2.35.1'
parses '2.35.1' and determines it is below the minimum 2.38
returns error with message 'requires git >= 2.38, found 2.35.1' to the hub startup routine
receives non-nil error and halts startup with the actionable error message
calls GitRunner.Run(ctx, 'merge-tree', '--write-tree', ...) with a context that is subsequently cancelled
starts 'git merge-tree --write-tree ...' subprocess via exec.CommandContext
cancels the context before the subprocess completes
sends SIGKILL to the git subprocess immediately
returns (partialStdout, partialStderr, error) where error wraps the context cancellation; caller handles err != nil alongside any partial output

error_handling.condition: git exits with a non-zero exit code during Run
error_handling.behavior: Run returns a *GitError with Command (joined args without binary prefix), ExitCode, and Stderr fields; Error() produces 'git <args> exited with code <N>: <stderr>'

error_handling.condition: git binary not found on PATH during Run
error_handling.behavior: Run returns the raw *exec.Error from os/exec directly without wrapping in GitError; this is a host misconfiguration

error_handling.condition: context cancelled or timed out during Run
error_handling.behavior: exec.CommandContext sends SIGKILL immediately; Run returns partial stdout/stderr alongside the context error; both err != nil and len(stdout) > 0 may be true simultaneously

error_handling.condition: system-level failure (binary not found, context cancelled) during RunExitCode
error_handling.behavior: RunExitCode returns err != nil wrapped via fmt.Errorf("%w", ...) preserving the underlying os/exec error for errors.Is/errors.As; exitCode is raw diagnostic context only; no GitError is produced

error_handling.condition: SIGKILL signal termination during RunExitCode due to context cancellation
error_handling.behavior: RunExitCode returns err != nil and exitCode == -1 (Go's exec.ExitError.ExitCode() for signal termination); partial stdout/stderr are returned alongside the error

error_handling.condition: git ls-remote exits with non-zero, non-2 exit code during BranchExists
error_handling.behavior: BranchExists returns (false, error) describing the network/auth/system failure; the failure is never misinterpreted as branch-missing

error_handling.condition: context deadline expires during BranchExists against a slow or unreachable remote
error_handling.behavior: SIGKILL is sent to the git subprocess; BranchExists returns (false, error) wrapping the context error

error_handling.condition: installed git version is below 2.38 when CheckGitVersion is called
error_handling.behavior: CheckGitVersion returns an error with the exact format 'requires git >= 2.38, found <installed>'

error_handling.condition: git --version output cannot be parsed into three numeric components
error_handling.behavior: CheckGitVersion returns a parse error describing the unparseable version string

error_handling.condition: git binary not found on PATH during CheckGitVersion
error_handling.behavior: CheckGitVersion returns the raw os/exec error without wrapping in GitError

error_handling.condition: workDir does not exist when Run or RunExitCode is called
error_handling.behavior: the raw os/exec working-directory error is returned as-is; no GitError is produced for this host misconfiguration

symbols.name: Command
symbols.notes: Used to construct git subprocess commands; Cmd.Env is set explicitly with the deduplicated environment.

symbols.name: CommandContext
symbols.signature: func CommandContext(ctx context.Context, name string, arg ...string) *Cmd
symbols.notes: Used instead of Command when context cancellation/timeout support is needed; sends SIGKILL on context cancellation by default.

symbols.name: ExitError
symbols.notes: Returned by Cmd.Run when the process exits with a non-zero status; ExitCode() returns -1 for signal termination.

symbols.name: ExitError.ExitCode
symbols.notes: Returns the exit code of the process; returns -1 if the process was killed by a signal.

symbols.name: Error
symbols.signature: type Error struct { Name string; Err error }
symbols.notes: Returned when the binary is not found on PATH; used to distinguish host misconfiguration from git-level failures.
